answer.rationale: The incumbent has refused to reopen pricing and the mandate is 18% spend reduction. memory_c2 confirms the low-cost vendor executed successfully on onboarding and invoicing accuracy in a prior switch. The low-cost vendor's quote meets the mandate alone. However, at 94% line utilization with no buffer, a single-source dependency creates supply risk. A standard_experiment with the low-cost vendor as primary addresses the financial mandate immediately while we retain the incumbent option post-decision. memory_c4 shows renegotiation recovered margin when benchmarked; that tactic is now unavailable (incumbent refused). Deferring defers the hard constraint. Adding a second source does not meet the cost mandate in one cycle. Switching to the low-cost vendor is the only option that satisfies both the financial mandate and keeps the line running, though it elevates execution risk during the transition and leaves zero redundancy. The verification of memory_c2 confirms the vendor can execute the onboarding and accuracy requirements this organization requires.
